meta.title: A second weather year for Prairie Town: hourly shapes from SPP, 2024 (29 February left out)
meta.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-930 Hourly Electric Grid Monitor, six-month BALANCE files (on the Grid Monitor's dashboard: Download Data → Six-Month Files), balancing authority SWPP (Southwest Power Pool), calendar year 2024
meta.license: EIA data are U.S. government works in the public domain; derived profiles CC BY 4.0
meta.normalisation: the cleaning rules of town_year.json (the Prairie Town data build step), applied to 2024; demand / 2024 peak hourly demand; wind and solar / their own 2024 maximum hourly output; integers in thousandths; EIA adjusted values; the 24 hours of 29 February (UTC-6) left out, so index i is the hour starting i hours after 00:00 on 1 January, Central standard time, skipping 29 February
meta.built_by: the M3 weather-year data build step

dataset.creator: Honglin Li
dataset.status: Real data, cleaned and rescaled: SPP's 2024 hourly demand, wind and solar (EIA-930), 29 February left out; repaired hours are counted in stats.
dataset.source: Extracted from EIA's Form EIA-930 six-month BALANCE files for 2024 (file names and SHA-256 checksums in meta) and cleaned by the rules in meta.normalisation.
dataset.license: Derived profiles: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), Honglin Li. The underlying EIA-930 data are U.S. government works in the public domain.
